1.below: Counts to around 20 reliably; needs support beyond and when crossing tens; counts in 10s with prompts.
1.meeting: Counts to and across 100, forwards and backwards, from any given number; counts in 2s, 5s and 10s.
1.exceeding: Counts fluently across 100 from any starting number, including over tens boundaries, and predicts what comes next.

1.below: Reads and writes some numbers to 20; matches some numbers to objects/pictures with support.
1.meeting: Identifies and represents numbers using objects and pictures; reads and writes numbers to 100 in numerals and 1–20 in words.
1.exceeding: Represents the same number in several ways and explains which representation is clearest; writes number words accurately.

1.below: Finds one more / one less within 10 using apparatus.
1.meeting: Given a number, identifies one more and one less.
1.exceeding: Reasons about one more / one less across tens boundaries and explains the pattern.

1.below: Knows some number bonds within 10; counts on / back with apparatus.
1.meeting: Adds and subtracts one- and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero.
1.exceeding: Recalls bonds within 20 fluently and uses them to derive related facts.

1.below: Solves one-step problems with objects and adult support.
1.meeting: Solves one-step addition and subtraction problems with concrete objects and pictures, and missing-number problems (e.g. 7 = □ − 9).
1.exceeding: Explains the strategy chosen and solves simple two-step or missing-number problems independently.

1.below: Shares and groups practically with support.
1.meeting: Solves one-step multiplication and division problems using objects, pictures and arrays with teacher support.
1.exceeding: Recognises equal groups and links them to counting in 2s, 5s and 10s, explaining the connection.

1.below: Finds halves of shapes with support; not yet sure parts must be equal.
1.meeting: Recognises, finds and names a half and a quarter of an object, shape or quantity.
1.exceeding: Finds halves and quarters of quantities and spots non-examples where the parts are unequal.

1.below: Fills missing-number gaps within 10 using apparatus.
1.meeting: Solves missing-number problems such as 7 = □ − 9 using addition and subtraction.
1.exceeding: Explains how the missing number was found and checks it by working backwards.

1.below: Compares two items directly with support; begins to use non-standard units.
1.meeting: Compares, describes and solves practical problems for length, mass, capacity and time, and begins to measure and record.
1.exceeding: Measures with uniform units accurately and reasons about which item is longer / heavier / holds more and why.

1.below: Recognises a few common coins with prompts.
1.meeting: Recognises and knows the value of different coins and notes.
1.exceeding: Orders coins by value and finds simple totals of two coins.

1.below: Uses some time language; reads o’clock with support.
1.meeting: Sequences events chronologically; uses date language; tells the time to the hour and half past and draws the hands.
1.exceeding: Tells o’clock and half past confidently and reasons about what happens before / after a given time.

1.meeting: Recognises and names common 2-D shapes (rectangles incl. squares, circles, triangles).
1.exceeding: Sorts 2-D shapes and begins to describe why, referring to sides and corners.

1.meeting: Recognises and names common 3-D shapes (cuboids incl. cubes, pyramids, spheres).
1.exceeding: Matches 3-D shapes to real-world objects and sorts them by simple properties.

1.below: Follows whole / half turn instructions with support.
1.meeting: Describes position, direction and movement, including whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.
1.exceeding: Uses turn and positional language precisely to give and follow directions.

2.below: Counts in 2s, 5s and 10s from 0; insecure in 3s and from other numbers.
2.meeting: Counts in steps of 2, 3 and 5 from 0, and in 10s from any number, forwards and backwards.
2.exceeding: Counts confidently in all steps from any number and uses the pattern to predict later terms.

2.below: Reads and writes some numbers to 100 in numerals; words insecure.
2.meeting: Reads and writes numbers to at least 100 in numerals and words.
2.exceeding: Writes number words accurately and represents a number several ways, explaining each.

2.below: Partitions two-digit numbers with apparatus; compares using objects.
2.meeting: Recognises the place value of each digit in a two-digit number; compares and orders 0–100 using <, > and =.
2.exceeding: Partitions flexibly (e.g. 34 = 20 + 14) and reasons about comparison and ordering statements.

2.below: Uses number facts to solve simple problems with support.
2.meeting: Uses place value and number facts to solve problems.
2.exceeding: Chooses efficient facts and explains reasoning in unfamiliar problems.

2.below: Secure with bonds to 20; insecure when crossing a tens boundary.
2.meeting: Adds and subtracts (concrete, pictorial, mental): a two-digit number and ones; and tens; two two-digit numbers; three one-digit numbers.
2.exceeding: Crosses tens boundaries fluently and selects the most efficient strategy.

2.below: Solves one-step problems with apparatus.
2.meeting: Solves addition and subtraction problems with objects / pictures (incl. quantities and measures), applying mental and written methods.
2.exceeding: Solves multi-step and missing-number problems and explains the method.

2.below: Counts in 2s, 5s and 10s; recall of facts not secure.
2.meeting: Recalls and uses 2, 5 and 10 facts; recognises odd / even; understands × is commutative and ÷ is not.
2.exceeding: Has rapid recall; reasons about commutativity and uses the inverse.

2.below: Writes simple statements with support.
2.meeting: Calculates and writes ×, ÷ and = statements within known tables.
2.exceeding: Writes families of related multiplication and division facts and explains the links.

2.below: Uses arrays / repeated addition with support.
2.meeting: Solves multiplication and division problems using arrays, repeated addition and known facts in context.
2.exceeding: Solves scaling, correspondence and missing-number problems and explains.

2.below: Finds halves and quarters of shapes; quantities with support.
2.meeting: Recognises, finds, names and writes 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set or quantity.
2.exceeding: Finds thirds and three-quarters of quantities and finds non-unit fractions of amounts.

2.below: Recognises 1/2 and 2/4 as the same with diagrams.
2.meeting: Recognises the equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2.
2.exceeding: Reasons about other simple equivalences using diagrams.

2.below: Writes simple fractions of amounts with support.
2.meeting: Writes simple fractions (e.g. 1/2 of 6 = 3).
2.exceeding: Links finding a fraction of an amount to division and explains.

2.below: Checks a calculation using the inverse with prompts.
2.meeting: Recognises and uses the inverse relationship between + and − to check calculations and solve missing-number problems.
2.exceeding: Uses the inverse independently to solve and justify a range of missing-number problems.

2.below: Measures with support; chooses units with help.
2.meeting: Chooses and uses standard units to estimate and measure length, mass, temperature and capacity; compares and orders using <, > and =.
2.exceeding: Selects appropriate units and justifies choices; reasons about comparisons.

2.below: Recognises £ and p; combines amounts with support.
2.meeting: Uses £ and p; combines amounts; finds different coin combinations; solves problems involving change (same unit).
2.exceeding: Finds change with several coins and explores all combinations to make a value.

2.below: Tells o’clock and half past; five-minute times with support.
2.meeting: Tells and writes the time to five minutes incl. quarter past / to; knows minutes in an hour and hours in a day.
2.exceeding: Calculates simple durations and reasons about start / end times.

2.below: Names shapes; states some properties with support.
2.meeting: Describes 2-D shape properties (sides, vertical line symmetry); identifies 2-D shapes on 3-D shapes; sorts 2-D shapes.
2.exceeding: Classifies by several properties and reasons about symmetry.

2.below: Names common 3-D shapes with prompts.
2.meeting: Recognises, names and sorts common 3-D shapes and everyday objects.
2.exceeding: Describes and compares 3-D shapes by faces, edges and vertices.

2.below: Continues a pattern; uses some position language with support.
2.meeting: Arranges objects in patterns / sequences; describes position, direction and rotation (quarter / half / three-quarter turns, clockwise / anti-clockwise).
2.exceeding: Uses precise rotational and positional language to describe and predict movement.

2.below: Reads simple charts with support.
2.meeting: Interprets and constructs pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and simple tables.
2.exceeding: Constructs accurate charts and chooses how to present categorical data.

2.below: Counts and sorts categories with support.
2.meeting: Asks and answers questions about totalling and comparing categorical data.
2.exceeding: Answers comparison and total questions and reasons about what the data shows.

3.below: Counts in some multiples with support; finds 10 more / less.
3.meeting: Counts in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s; finds 10 or 100 more / less.
3.exceeding: Counts fluently in all multiples and reasons about the effect of 10 / 100 more or less.

3.below: Reads / writes numbers to 1000 with support; estimating insecure.
3.meeting: Identifies, represents and estimates numbers using different representations; reads and writes to 1000 in numerals and words.
3.exceeding: Estimates and justifies positions on a number line and represents numbers in multiple ways.

3.meeting: Recognises place value in three-digit numbers; compares and orders to 1000.
3.exceeding: Reasons about place value and orders sets of numbers, explaining.

3.meeting: Solves number and practical problems involving these ideas.
3.exceeding: Solves multi-step and reasoning problems independently.

3.below: Mental ±; column method insecure when exchanging.
3.meeting: Adds / subtracts mentally (3-digit and ones / tens / hundreds); column add / sub up to three digits.
3.exceeding: Exchanges fluently and chooses mental or written methods efficiently.

3.below: Solves one-step problems; missing-number with support.
3.meeting: Solves problems, incl. missing-number, using number facts, place value and more complex ±.
3.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems, explains the method and checks.

3.meeting: Recalls and uses 3, 4 and 8 multiplication and division facts.
3.exceeding: Has secure recall; derives related facts and reasons.

3.meeting: Calculates statements incl. two-digit × one-digit, mental progressing to formal written.
3.exceeding: Uses the formal method confidently and explains the distributive idea.

3.meeting: Solves problems incl. missing-number, scaling and correspondence.
3.exceeding: Solves harder scaling / correspondence problems and explains.

3.below: Counts in tenths with prompts; unit fractions of sets with support.
3.meeting: Counts in tenths; finds and writes fractions of a set (unit and non-unit, small denom.); uses fractions as numbers.
3.exceeding: Finds non-unit fractions of amounts and reasons about tenths arising from dividing by 10.

3.below: Shows equivalent fractions with diagrams with support.
3.meeting: Shows equivalent fractions with diagrams; compares and orders unit fractions and same-denominator fractions.
3.exceeding: Reasons about equivalence and ordering without relying on diagrams.

3.meeting: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same denominator within one whole.
3.exceeding: Solves missing-number fraction calculations and explains.

3.below: Solves simple fraction problems with support.
3.meeting: Solves problems involving all of the above.
3.exceeding: Solves multi-step fraction problems and reasons.

3.below: Solves simple missing-number problems with support.
3.meeting: Solves problems, including missing number problems.
3.exceeding: Reasons about and explains a range of missing-number problems.

3.below: Measures and reads scales with support.
3.meeting: Measures, compares, adds and subtracts length (m/cm/mm), mass (kg/g) and capacity (l/ml).
3.exceeding: Converts within a measure and solves multi-step measure problems.

3.meeting: Adds and subtracts amounts of money to give change, using £ and p.
3.exceeding: Solves multi-step money problems and finds efficient ways to give change.

3.below: Tells time to five minutes; analogue reading developing.
3.meeting: Tells / writes time on analogue (incl. Roman numerals) and 12 / 24-hour clocks to the minute; knows seconds, days, months; compares durations.
3.exceeding: Reads all clocks accurately and calculates durations across the hour.

3.below: Measures perimeter by counting with support.
3.meeting: Measures the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
3.exceeding: Reasons about perimeter and finds missing side lengths.

3.meeting: Draws 2-D shapes.
3.exceeding: Draws shapes accurately and describes their properties.

3.meeting: Makes 3-D shapes with modelling materials; recognises and describes 3-D shapes in different orientations.
3.exceeding: Describes 3-D shapes by faces, edges and vertices and relates them to 2-D faces.

3.meeting: Recognises angles as turns; identifies right angles and compares to a right angle; identifies horizontal / vertical, perpendicular / parallel lines.
3.exceeding: Reasons about turns and classifies lines and angles accurately.

3.meeting: Interprets and presents data using bar charts, pictograms and tables.
3.exceeding: Constructs accurate scaled charts and chooses scales.

3.meeting: Solves one- and two-step questions (e.g. ‘how many more / fewer?’) from scaled charts, pictograms and tables.
3.exceeding: Answers two-step and comparison questions and reasons from the data.

4.below: Counts in some multiples; negative numbers insecure.
4.meeting: Counts in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1000s; counts back through zero (negatives).
4.exceeding: Counts fluently incl. through zero and reasons about negative values.

4.below: Reads Roman numerals to 100 with support.
4.meeting: Represents / estimates numbers in different ways; reads Roman numerals to 100 and knows about the concept of zero and place value.
4.exceeding: Converts confidently to / from Roman numerals and explains the historical change.

4.below: Reads / writes four-digit numbers with support.
4.meeting: Finds 1000 more / less; recognises four-digit place value; orders and compares beyond 1000.
4.exceeding: Reasons about four-digit place value and orders large sets, explaining.

4.below: Rounds to 10 / 100 with prompts.
4.meeting: Rounds to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000; solves problems with increasingly large positive numbers.
4.exceeding: Reasons about rounding and solves multi-step problems.

4.below: Column methods insecure with exchanges.
4.meeting: Adds / subtracts up to four digits using formal column methods where appropriate.
4.exceeding: Selects efficient methods and uses estimation / inverse to check.

4.below: Solves one-step problems.
4.meeting: Solves two-step problems in context, deciding which operations and methods to use.
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems and justifies the approach.

4.below: Recall of tables to 12 × 12 developing.
4.meeting: Recalls tables to 12 × 12; uses place value / derived facts (×0, ×1, ÷1, × three numbers); factor pairs and commutativity.
4.exceeding: Fluent recall; reasons with factor pairs and uses derived facts flexibly.

4.below: Two- / three-digit × one-digit with support.
4.meeting: Multiplies two- and three-digit numbers by a one-digit number using formal written layout.
4.exceeding: Uses the method fluently and estimates to check.

4.below: Solves simple × / + problems with support.
4.meeting: Solves problems with multiplying and adding, the distributive law, integer scaling and harder correspondence.
4.exceeding: Applies the distributive law flexibly and solves harder scaling problems.

4.below: Counts in hundredths with prompts.
4.meeting: Counts in hundredths; knows hundredths arise from dividing by 100 and tenths by ten.
4.exceeding: Relates tenths, hundredths and division and explains.

4.below: Shows equivalent fractions with diagrams with support.
4.meeting: Shows families of common equivalent fractions using diagrams.
4.exceeding: Generates equivalent fractions and reasons about the pattern.

4.below: Adds same-denominator fractions with support.
4.meeting: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same denominator.
4.exceeding: Solves missing-number fraction calculations and explains.

4.below: Finds simple fractions of quantities with support.
4.meeting: Solves problems with harder fractions of quantities and dividing quantities (incl. non-unit, whole-number answers).
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step fraction problems and reasons.

4.below: Relates simple fractions and decimals with support.
4.meeting: Writes decimal equivalents of tenths / hundredths and of 1/4, 1/2, 3/4; rounds 1 d.p. to the whole; compares to 2 d.p.
4.exceeding: Reasons about decimal place value and orders decimals confidently.

4.below: Solves simple measure / money problems with support.
4.meeting: Solves simple measure and money problems involving fractions and decimals to 2 d.p.
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step measure / money problems with decimals and explains.

4.below: Converts simple units with support.
4.meeting: Converts between units (e.g. km–m, hour–minute); estimates, compares and calculates measures.
4.exceeding: Converts confidently and solves multi-step measure problems.

4.below: Calculates with money with support.
4.meeting: Estimates, compares and calculates measures, including money in £ and p.
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step money problems and reasons about value.

4.below: Reads 12 / 24-hour time with support.
4.meeting: Reads, writes and converts time between analogue and 12 / 24-hour digital; solves conversion problems (hr→min, etc.).
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step time problems across formats.

4.below: Finds perimeter / area by counting with support.
4.meeting: Measures / calculates the perimeter of a rectilinear figure; finds area by counting squares.
4.exceeding: Reasons about area and perimeter and finds missing lengths.

4.below: Classifies common shapes with support; finds a vertical line of symmetry.
4.meeting: Compares and classifies quadrilaterals and triangles by properties / size; identifies lines of symmetry in different orientations.
4.exceeding: Classifies by multiple properties and reasons about symmetry in any orientation.

4.below: Identifies acute / obtuse with prompts; completes symmetry with support.
4.meeting: Identifies acute and obtuse angles; orders angles to two right angles; completes a symmetric figure to a given line.
4.exceeding: Reasons about and orders angles and completes symmetric figures accurately.

4.below: Plots points in the first quadrant with support.
4.meeting: Describes first-quadrant coordinates; describes translations; plots points and completes a polygon.
4.exceeding: Uses coordinates and translations accurately and predicts positions.

4.below: Reads bar charts / tables with support.
4.meeting: Interprets and presents discrete and continuous data, incl. bar charts and time graphs.
4.exceeding: Selects appropriate graphs / scales and interprets time graphs.

4.below: Answers simple data questions with support.
4.meeting: Solves comparison, sum and difference problems using various graphs.
4.exceeding: Solves multi-step data problems and reasons.

5.below: Counts in powers of 10 with support.
5.meeting: Counts forwards / backwards in steps of powers of 10 for any number up to 1,000,000.
5.exceeding: Reasons about the effect of adding / subtracting powers of 10.

5.below: Reads / writes large numbers with support; Roman numerals to 1000 developing.
5.meeting: Reads, writes and determines the value of each digit to 1,000,000; reads Roman numerals to 1000 and recognises years.
5.exceeding: Represents large numbers in multiple ways and explains digit values.

5.below: Orders large numbers with support.
5.meeting: Orders and compares numbers to at least 1,000,000 and determines digit values.
5.exceeding: Reasons about ordering and comparison of large numbers.

5.below: Rounds with prompts; negatives insecure.
5.meeting: Interprets negatives in context; rounds to the nearest 10 up to 100,000; solves problems involving all of the above.
5.exceeding: Reasons about rounding and negatives and solves multi-step problems.

5.below: Column methods insecure with larger numbers.
5.meeting: Adds / subtracts numbers with more than four digits (formal written); mentally with increasingly large numbers.
5.exceeding: Selects efficient methods and uses estimation / inverse to check.

5.below: Solves one- / two-step problems.
5.meeting: Solves multi-step problems in context, deciding operations and methods.
5.exceeding: Solves complex multi-step problems and justifies.

5.below: Identifies factors / multiples with support; primes / squares developing.
5.meeting: Identifies multiples, factors and common factors; primes (recall to 19, test to 100), composites; square and cube numbers.
5.exceeding: Reasons with factors, primes, squares and cubes and explains.

5.below: Long multiplication / short division with support.
5.meeting: × up to 4-digit by 1- / 2-digit (incl. long mult.); ÷ up to 4-digit by 1-digit (short division) with remainders; ×÷ by 10 / 100 / 1000 incl. decimals.
5.exceeding: Uses formal methods fluently and interprets remainders in context.

5.below: Solves simple ×÷ problems with support.
5.meeting: Solves problems using knowledge of factors, multiples, squares and cubes.
5.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems and reasons about the most efficient approach.

5.below: Applies the equals sign in simple combined problems with support.
5.meeting: Solves problems with +, −, × and ÷ combined, understanding the meaning of =.
5.exceeding: Solves multi-step combined problems and explains the order used.

5.below: Finds equivalent fractions / converts with support.
5.meeting: Writes equivalent fractions (incl. tenths / hundredths); converts between mixed numbers and improper fractions; writes statements > 1 as mixed numbers.
5.exceeding: Reasons about equivalence and converts fluently both ways.

5.below: Compares fractions with related denominators with support.
5.meeting: Compares and orders fractions whose denominators are multiples of the same number.
5.exceeding: Compares and orders a wider range of fractions by reasoning.

5.below: Adds related-denominator fractions with support.
5.meeting: Adds / subtracts fractions (same and multiple denominators); multiplies proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers.
5.exceeding: Calculates fluently and solves missing-number fraction problems.

5.below: Reads / writes decimals to 3 d.p. with support.
5.meeting: Writes decimals as fractions; uses thousandths; rounds to whole and 1 d.p.; reads, writes, orders and compares to 3 d.p.
5.exceeding: Reasons about decimal place value and rounding to 3 d.p.

5.below: Relates % to fractions / decimals with support.
5.meeting: Understands %; writes % as a fraction (denom. 100) and a decimal; solves problems with % / decimal equivalents of common fractions.
5.exceeding: Reasons across fraction–decimal–percentage equivalents in unfamiliar contexts.

5.below: Converts metric units with support.
5.meeting: Converts metric units; uses approximate metric–imperial equivalences; uses four operations to solve measure problems (incl. scaling) with decimals.
5.exceeding: Converts confidently and solves multi-step measure problems with scaling.

5.below: Solves money problems with support.
5.meeting: Uses all four operations to solve problems involving money.
5.exceeding: Solves multi-step money problems and reasons about efficiency.

5.below: Converts between units of time with support.
5.meeting: Solves problems involving converting between units of time.
5.exceeding: Solves multi-step time-conversion problems.

5.below: Finds perimeter / area of rectangles with support.
5.meeting: Perimeter of composite shapes; area of rectangles (cm² / m²) and estimate of irregular areas; estimates volume and capacity.
5.exceeding: Reasons about area, perimeter and volume and solves multi-step problems.

5.below: Identifies regular / irregular polygons with support.
5.meeting: Distinguishes regular / irregular polygons by reasoning; uses rectangle properties to find missing lengths / angles.
5.exceeding: Reasons about properties to deduce a chain of related facts.

5.below: Identifies 3-D shapes from 2-D with support.
5.meeting: Identifies 3-D shapes, incl. cubes and other cuboids, from 2-D representations.
5.exceeding: Visualises and reasons about 3-D shapes from different 2-D views.

5.below: Measures / draws angles with support.
5.meeting: Knows angles in degrees; estimates / compares acute, obtuse, reflex; draws and measures angles; identifies angles at a point / straight line / multiples of 90°.
5.exceeding: Measures and draws accurately and reasons about angle facts.

5.below: Reflects / translates simple shapes with support.
5.meeting: Identifies, describes and represents position after reflection or translation; knows the shape is unchanged.
5.exceeding: Describes reflections / translations precisely and predicts the image.

5.below: Reads tables / timetables with support.
5.meeting: Completes, reads and interprets information in tables, including timetables.
5.exceeding: Interprets timetables and extracts information to solve problems.

5.below: Reads line graphs with support.
5.meeting: Solves comparison, sum and difference problems using a line graph.
5.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems from line graphs and reasons.

6.below: Counts through zero with support.
6.meeting: Counts forwards and backwards with positive and negative whole numbers, including through zero.
6.exceeding: Reasons about intervals across zero and predicts terms.

6.below: Reads / writes numbers to 10,000,000 with support.
6.meeting: Reads, writes and determines the value of each digit up to 10,000,000.
6.exceeding: Represents very large numbers in multiple ways and explains digit values.

6.below: Orders large numbers with support.
6.meeting: Orders and compares numbers up to 10,000,000 and determines digit values.
6.exceeding: Reasons about ordering and comparison of very large numbers.

6.below: Rounds and uses negatives with prompts.
6.meeting: Rounds to a required degree of accuracy; uses negatives in context; calculates intervals across zero; solves problems with all of the above.
6.exceeding: Reasons about rounding / accuracy and solves multi-step problems.

6.below: Identifies common factors / multiples / primes with support; estimates with prompts.
6.meeting: Identifies common factors, common multiples and primes; uses estimation to check and to choose an appropriate degree of accuracy.
6.exceeding: Reasons with factors / multiples / primes and judges sensible accuracy.

6.below: Long methods insecure.
6.meeting: Long multiplication (4-digit × 2-digit); long and short division with remainders interpreted appropriately; mental with mixed operations.
6.exceeding: Uses formal methods fluently and interprets remainders flexibly.

6.below: Solves single-operation problems with support.
6.meeting: Solves problems involving +, −, × and ÷.
6.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems and chooses efficient methods.

6.below: Applies the order of operations with support.
6.meeting: Uses the order of operations to carry out calculations involving the four operations.
6.exceeding: Applies the order of operations fluently to multi-step calculations and explains.

6.below: Simplifies / finds common denominators with support.
6.meeting: Simplifies fractions with common factors; uses common multiples for common denominators; compares and orders fractions incl. > 1.
6.exceeding: Reasons about equivalence and orders a wide range of fractions.

6.below: Adds different-denominator fractions with support.
6.meeting: Adds / subtracts fractions with different denominators and mixed numbers; multiplies pairs of proper fractions (simplest form); divides proper fractions by whole numbers.
6.exceeding: Calculates fluently across all four operations on fractions and explains.

6.below: Identifies digit value to 3 d.p. with support.
6.meeting: Identifies the value of each digit in numbers to three decimal places.
6.exceeding: Reasons about decimal place value to 3 d.p.

6.below: Relates fractions, decimals and percentages with prompts.
6.meeting: Associates a fraction with division and finds decimal equivalents (e.g. 0.375); recalls and uses FDP equivalences in different contexts.
6.exceeding: Moves fluently between fractions, decimals and percentages and reasons in unfamiliar contexts.

6.below: Solves simple ratio / scaling problems with support.
6.meeting: Solves relative-size problems (integer ×÷); percentages for comparison; similar shapes / scale factor; unequal sharing and grouping using fractions and multiples.
6.exceeding: Reasons proportionally and solves multi-step ratio, percentage and scaling problems.

6.below: Uses simple formulae and continues sequences with support.
6.meeting: Uses simple formulae; generates / describes linear sequences; expresses missing-number problems algebraically; finds pairs satisfying an equation with two unknowns; enumerates combinations.
6.exceeding: Reasons algebraically, generalises rules and works systematically with two unknowns.

6.below: Converts units with support.
6.meeting: Solves conversion problems using decimal notation to 3 d.p.; converts between standard units (length, mass, volume, time); miles–km.
6.exceeding: Converts confidently to 3 d.p. and solves multi-step measure problems.

6.below: Converts time units with support.
6.meeting: Converts time between standard units (smaller ↔ larger). Note: WRM covers most time conversion in Y5.
6.exceeding: Solves multi-step problems combining time and other measures.

6.below: Uses area / volume formulae with support.
6.meeting: Knows when to use formulae; area of parallelograms and triangles; volume of cubes / cuboids (cm³ / m³); same area ≠ same perimeter.
6.exceeding: Reasons about area, perimeter and volume and solves multi-step problems.

6.below: Draws shapes and names circle parts with support.
6.meeting: Draws 2-D shapes from dimensions / angles; classifies shapes; names parts of circles (radius, diameter, circumference) and knows diameter = 2 × radius.
6.exceeding: Reasons about properties and circle relationships accurately.

6.below: Builds 3-D shapes / nets with support.
6.meeting: Recognises, describes and builds simple 3-D shapes, including making nets.
6.exceeding: Visualises nets and reasons about which fold into a given solid.

6.below: Finds simple missing angles with support.
6.meeting: Finds unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons; recognises angles at a point, on a straight line and vertically opposite.
6.exceeding: Reasons through multi-step angle problems using known facts.

6.below: Works in the first quadrant with support.
